issues.legal_issue: A ghatwali tenure is dependent on a zamindary rather than a government tenure when the evidence, considered as a whole, supports its connection with the zamindary and does not clearly establish its creation by the government.
material_facts: The tenure was included in the zamindary settlement and was covered by the rent assessed on the zamindary.
The record of rights described the tenure as held under the zamindar.
The historical sanad concerned ghatwari duties and did not itself grant land or establish that the tenure was created by the government.
The evidence relied on to establish a government tenure, including notices and receipts, did not clearly show that the holder acted as a government ghatwal.
issues.conclusion: The tenure was a zamindary ghatwali, not a government ghatwali, and the evidence did not rebut the inference arising from its inclusion in the zamindary settlement and its description in the record of rights.
issues.legal_principle: A government ghatwali is created by the ruling power for services to it, while a zamindary ghatwali is created by a zamindar for services to the zamindar. Inclusion in a zamindary settlement and coverage by its assessed rent supports a connection with the zamindary, though settlement alone does not determine the nature of the tenure or convert public services into private ones (Raja Lelanund Singh Bahadoor v. The Bengal Government; Raja Nilmoni Singh v. Bakranath Singh). Where the evidence does not clearly establish the tenure’s true character, inclusion in the zamindary and coverage by its assessed rent can tip the balance in favour of dependence on the zamindary. A District Gazetteer is not conclusive but is an official document of evidentiary value; the character of a tenure is not changed merely because it is described as being under the Collector. The judgment also considers Fulbati Kumari v. Maheshwari Prasad and Rani Sonabati Kumari v. Raja Kirtyanand Singh in discussing the historical evidence and nature of ghatwali tenures.

rule.if: civil_appeal and tenure_included_in_zamindary_settlement and record_shows_tenure_under_zamindar and government_origin_not_clearly_established

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal challenging the classification of a tenure.
predicates.tenure_included_in_zamindary_settlement: The tenure was included in a zamindary settlement and covered by the rent assessed on that zamindary.
predicates.record_shows_tenure_under_zamindar: The record of rights described the tenure as held under the zamindar.
predicates.government_origin_not_clearly_establishe: The evidence did not clearly establish that the government created the tenure.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a tenure included in a zamindary settlement, the record places it under the zamindar, and government creation is not clearly established, the tenure is treated as dependent on the zamindary.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of acquisition of mineral rights by adverse possession fails where the concurrent factual findings do not establish the required possession and no exceptional basis warrants reopening those findings on appeal.
material_facts: The courts below found no clear evidence that a mine had been worked on behalf of the alleged holders of the rights.
The evidence showed, at most, isolated acts of possession in recent years.
The findings on adverse possession were concurrent, and the appellant did not establish exceptional circumstances warranting their reconsideration.
issues.conclusion: The plea of adverse possession was not established, and the concurrent findings against it were left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court is ordinarily reluctant to reinvestigate matters fully considered by the courts below where their findings are concurrent; absent exceptional circumstances, those findings stand. The evidence of isolated recent acts, without clear proof of mining possession, did not sustain the plea of adverse possession.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal challenging findings made by the courts below.
predicates.concurrent_findings_against_adverse_poss: Both courts below found against the claim that the rights had been acquired by adverse possession.
predicates.evidence_shows_only_isolated_recent_poss: The evidence showed at most isolated acts of possession in recent years and did not clearly establish sustained working of the mines.
predicates.no_exceptional_basis_to_reopen: The appellant did not show exceptional circumstances justifying reconsideration of the concurrent findings.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, adverse possession is not established where both lower courts rejected the claim, the evidence shows only isolated recent possession, and no exceptional basis for reopening their findings is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A suit for recovery is not barred by limitation where the trial court found possession within the applicable limitation period and that finding is not shown to lack evidentiary support.
material_facts: The trial judge expressly found that the plaintiff had been in possession of the disputed land, including the land containing the mines, within the applicable limitation period.
The finding was not shown to have been challenged before the High Court.
The appellant did not contend that there was no evidence supporting possession within the applicable period.
issues.conclusion: The limitation plea was rejected because the finding of possession within the applicable period stood and was not shown to be unsupported by evidence.
issues.legal_principle: For the limitation contention raised under Articles 142 and 144 of the Limitation Act, the Court relied on the trial court’s finding of possession and the absence of a showing that the finding lacked evidentiary support. The judgment did not disturb that finding where it had not been challenged before the High Court and the appellant did not establish that there was no evidence for it.

rule.if: civil_appeal and recovery_suit and trial_court_found_possession_within_applicable_period and finding_not_shown_to_lack_evidence

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal challenging a limitation ruling in a suit for recovery.
predicates.recovery_suit: The underlying suit sought recovery of possession of disputed land.
predicates.trial_court_found_possession_within_appl: The trial court found that the claimant had possessed the disputed land within the applicable limitation period.
predicates.finding_not_shown_to_lack_evidence: The finding was not shown to have been challenged below or to lack evidentiary support.

issues.definition: A recovery suit is not barred by limitation when the trial court found possession within the applicable period and that finding is not shown to lack evidentiary support.

issues.legal_issue: A zamindar is presumed to own underground mineral rights in tenancies created by the zamindar unless there is evidence that the zamindar parted with those rights.
material_facts: The tenure was found to be a zamindary ghatwali.
The plaintiff acquired the tenure through a mortgage sale.
There was no evidence that the zamindar had parted with the underground rights.
The courts below found that the proprietor retained the subsoil rights.
issues.conclusion: The proprietor was entitled to the underground mineral rights; additionally, the tenure had passed to the plaintiff through the sale.
issues.legal_principle: A zamindar is presumed to own underground rights in tenancies created by the zamindar unless evidence shows that those rights were parted with. The Court relied on Hari Narayan Singh v. Sriram Chakravarthi and Durga Prasad Singh v. Braja Nath Bose. It also held that the entire tenure passed to the plaintiff by the sale.

rule.if: civil_appeal and tenancy_created_by_zamindar and no_evidence_zamindar_parted_with_mineral_rights and tenure_transferred_by_sale

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal concerning title to underground mineral rights.
predicates.tenancy_created_by_zamindar: The disputed tenancy was created by a zamindar.
predicates.no_evidence_zamindar_parted_with_mineral: There was no evidence that the zamindar had parted with the underground mineral rights.
predicates.tenure_transferred_by_sale: The tenure was transferred to the claimant through a sale.

issues.definition: Where a tenancy created by a zamindar is transferred by sale and there is no evidence that the zamindar parted with the mineral rights, the proprietor is entitled to those underground rights.
